about: When each 1904 Prairie Avenue house a jaunt stops at was torn down, as the district's 'Lost Houses' markers and the Encyclopedia of Chicago give it. The owner, 2026-11-07: when a jaunt has hit a building, somewhere in the stop, if it was torn down, mention that and, if appropriate, the context, without distracting heavily from the tour. tools/jaunt_built_so_far.py writes `line` into the build-log walk; every hand-written 1904 stop at one of these houses must give `year` in its text and cite a claim on `source` (tools/check_jaunt_demolitions.py, in check.sh). Only main houses are listed: no record read gives a coach house's own date. Houses not listed either survive or have no loss date read in 4D.

goodman_house_1612_prairie.claim: Joseph Goodman Residence, 1612 S. Prairie Avenue: razed circa 1960.

shortall_gregory_house_1638_prairie_fron.claim: John G. Shortall-Robert B. Gregory Residence, 1638 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1944.

hibbard_house_1701_prairie.line: RAZED 1932; from 1921 Louis Sullivan kept a free office here until his death in 1924.
hibbard_house_1701_prairie.claim: William G. Hibbard Residence, 1701 S. Prairie Avenue: in 1921 the house was bought by the American Terra Cotta & Ceramic Co., which gave the architect Louis Sullivan free office space there until his death in 1924. Razed 1932.

walker_house_1720_prairie.line: TORN DOWN 1910, the first of many Prairie Avenue houses to go.
walker_house_1720_prairie.claim: In 1910 wreckers destroyed the mansion at 1720 Prairie, the first of many Prairie Avenue homes to be torn down, as the street's residences increasingly gave way to offices, warehouses and factories.
walker_house_1720_prairie.locator: The essay's closing paragraphs on the street's decline.

dexter_house_1721_prairie.claim: Wirt Dexter Residence, 1721 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1927.

pullman_house_1729_prairie.claim: George M. Pullman Residence, 1729 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1922.

keith_house_1808_prairie.line: RAZED 1968, all but its north wall, kept to screen the Glessner courtyard.
keith_house_1808_prairie.claim: Osborn R. Keith Residence, 1808 S. Prairie Avenue: the north wall was retained during demolition in 1968 to preserve the private courtyard of the adjacent Glessner house.

wheeler_house_1812_prairie.claim: George H. Wheeler Residence, 1812 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1968.

sears_meeker_house_1815_prairie.claim: Joseph Sears Residence, 1815 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1967.

dent_house_1823_prairie.claim: Thomas Dent Residence, 1823 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1945.

marsh_house_1824_prairie.claim: Samuel B. Pomeroy Residence, 1824 S. Prairie Avenue: razed in the 1940s.
marsh_house_1824_prairie.locator: The 1824 S. Prairie Avenue entry and its photograph caption.

doane_house_1827_prairie.claim: John W. Doane Residence, 1827 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1936.

jones_house_1834_prairie.claim: Fernando Jones Residence, 1834 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1942.

ream_house_1901_prairie.line: RAZED 1929, after years as the Radford Architectural Company's offices.
ream_house_1901_prairie.claim: Osborn R. Keith-Norman B. Ream Residence, 1901 S. Prairie Avenue: the house later served as offices for the Radford Architectural Company. Razed 1929.

marshall_field_house_1905_prairie.line: RAZED 1955, after a spell as an aeronautical university.
marshall_field_house_1905_prairie.claim: Marshall Field Residence, 1905 S. Prairie Avenue: later converted to an aeronautical university. Razed 1955.

moulton_lowden_house_1912_prairie.claim: Bryan P. Moulton Residence, 1912 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1939.

mayer_house_2009_prairie.claim: Max A. Meyer Residence, 2009 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1955.

sherman_house_2100_prairie.claim: John B. Sherman Residence, 2100 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1936.

armour_house_2115_prairie.claim: David Kelley-Philip D. Armour Residence, 2115 S. Prairie Avenue: razed 1937.

robbins_house_2126_prairie.line: RAZED 2002, after years as the World Book Company's offices.
robbins_house_2126_prairie.claim: Edward F. Robbins Residence, 2126 S. Prairie Avenue: later occupied by the World Book Company. Razed 2002.

tucker_smith_house_2140_prairie.line: RAZED 1936; its dining room was taken apart first and rebuilt at the Northern Trust.
tucker_smith_house_2140_prairie.claim: William F. Tucker-Byron L. Smith Residence, 2140 S. Prairie Avenue: prior to demolition in 1936, the dining room was dismantled and reassembled as a private dining room at Northern Trust.
